ex.q: A student writes: 'With the SSID hidden, I don't need a Wi-Fi password.' Why is this dangerous?
ex.a:
1. Hidden SSIDs can still be found with sniffing tools.
2. Without encryption, anyone who finds it can join and read traffic.
3. Always keep WPA2 with a strong password; hiding is only an extra layer.
ex.az: 常见错误：隐藏 SSID 就不需密码。SSID 可被侦测，必须保留 WPA2 加密。

frames.en: The access point stores: …:AA (Dad's phone), …:BB (laptop).
frames.zh: AP 储存白名单。

frames.en: Device …:AA connects with the password → MAC on list → allowed.
frames.zh: AA 在名单 → 允许。

frames.en: Device …:CC has the correct password but its MAC is not on the list → rejected.
frames.zh: CC 不在名单 → 拒绝。

cards.en:
Analogy: using public Wi-Fi is like making a phone call in a crowded MTR carriage: anyone around can listen.

Why risky: anyone can connect, so hackers can join and monitor incoming and outgoing information. Data may be unencrypted. A fake hotspot (evil twin) may be used for MITM.

Safe practice:

  • General browsing only; avoid online banking, shopping and typing passwords.
  • Use HTTPS sites and a VPN.
  • Turn off auto-connect and file sharing.
  • 'Forget' the network after use.
  • Use mobile data for sensitive tasks.

Exam wording: As anyone can connect to public networks, hackers may intrude into them and monitor the incoming and outgoing information.

Also in the book: mobile networks are safer than public Wi-Fi (in theory only the user and the ISP share the network). Devices auto-join networks in 'Saved Networks'; a hacker can fake a hotspot with the same name and password, so delete public Wi-Fi from Saved Networks after use. If public Wi-Fi must be used for sensitive data, use a VPN.
cards.zh:
比喻：用公共 Wi-Fi 像在挤迫港铁车厢讲电话，旁人都听到。

风险：任何人都可连接，黑客可加入并监察进出资料；数据可能未加密；可能是 evil twin 作 MITM。

安全做法：

  • 只作一般浏览，避免网银、购物、输入密码。
  • 用 HTTPS 及 VPN。
  • 关闭自动连接和文件共享。
  • 用后“忘记网络”。
  • 敏感事情用流动数据。

考试写法：As anyone can connect to public networks, hackers may intrude into them and monitor the incoming and outgoing information.

课本还提到：流动网络比公共 Wi-Fi 安全（理论上只有用户和 ISP 共用）。装置会自动连接「已储存网络」；黑客可伪造同名同密码热点，所以用完要把公共 Wi-Fi 从已储存网络删除。非用公共 Wi-Fi 传敏感资料不可时，要用 VPN。

ex.q: Why is public Wi-Fi dangerous even when it is fast and free?
ex.a:
1. Speed is not the issue.
2. Anyone, including hackers, can join and intercept traffic.
3. Data may be unencrypted.
ex.az: 风险在于任何人可接入、数据未加密。

ex.q: At the airport, Amy must check her bank balance urgently. Give TWO safe options.
ex.a:
1. Switch to mobile data instead of public Wi-Fi.
2. Or turn on a VPN and use the bank's HTTPS app/site.
ex.az: 用流动数据，或开 VPN + HTTPS。

ex.q: A student writes: 'The mall Wi-Fi asks for a password at a login page, so it is fully secure.' What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. The login page only controls who can use the hotspot; the password is often shared with everyone.
2. Other users (including hackers) on the same network can still try to monitor traffic.
3. Still use HTTPS/VPN for sensitive data.
ex.az: 常见错误：有登入页就安全。密码人人可得，其他用户仍可监察，要用 HTTPS/VPN。

ex.q: Why delete 'Mall_Free_WiFi' from Saved Networks after shopping?
ex.a: So the phone will not auto-connect later to a fake hotspot with the same name (evil twin) set up by a hacker.
ex.az: 以免日后自动连上黑客伪造的同名热点。

cards.en:
Analogy: your browser is the front door to the Internet. Settings are its locks.

Settings to use:

  • Disable 'Pop-ups and redirects': blocks unwanted ads and being sent to malicious sites.
  • Enable automatic update: patches (fixes) for software vulnerabilities (security holes) are installed quickly.
  • Manage plug-ins (extensions): install only trusted ones; remove suspicious ones. A browser that keeps showing ads may have a malicious plug-in / adware.
  • Block third-party cookies; turn on safe-browsing warnings.

Also update the OS and all software: attackers exploit known, unpatched vulnerabilities (like WannaCry).

Exam wording: Disable the 'Pop-ups and redirects' feature. Enable the automatic update function of the web browser to ensure software vulnerabilities are duly removed.

Ad blocker: browser plug-ins such as ad blockers can make browsing safer. Patch everything: antivirus, firewall, browser and OS all have vulnerabilities; install the latest patches quickly.
cards.zh:
比喻：浏览器是通往 Internet 的大门，设定就是门锁。

应用设定：

  • 停用“弹出式视窗及重新导向”：挡广告和被导向恶意网站。
  • 启用自动更新：尽快修补漏洞 (vulnerabilities)。
  • 管理插件 (plug-ins)：只装可信任的，移除可疑的；不断弹广告可能是恶意插件/adware。
  • 封锁第三方 cookies；启用安全浏览警告。

亦要更新 OS 和所有软件，攻击者利用已知未修补漏洞（如 WannaCry）。

考试写法：Disable the 'Pop-ups and redirects' feature. Enable the automatic update function of the web browser to ensure software vulnerabilities are duly removed.

广告拦截：浏览器插件如广告拦截器可提升安全。全部要修补：防毒、防火墙、浏览器、操作系统都有漏洞，要尽快安装最新修补程式。

ex.q: Jane's browser keeps opening ad pages after she installed a 'free video downloader' extension. Suggest two actions.
ex.a:
1. Remove/disable the suspicious plug-in.
2. Disable pop-ups and redirects.
3. (Also) scan with antivirus; update the browser.
ex.az: 移除插件、停用弹窗、扫描。

ex.q: Why does automatic browser update improve security?
ex.a:
1. Developers find vulnerabilities and release patches.
2. Hackers attack browsers that are not yet patched.
3. Auto update installs patches quickly, so the hole is closed.
ex.az: 自动更新尽快修补漏洞，黑客无法利用。

ex.q: A student writes: 'Turn off browser updates, because updates may bring viruses.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Official updates come from the developer and fix vulnerabilities.
2. Not updating leaves known holes open for attackers.
3. Correct: enable automatic update.
ex.az: 常见错误：关闭更新。官方更新是修补漏洞，应启用自动更新。

cards.en:
Analogy: someone quietly listening at your door while you talk on the phone. You keep talking. You never notice.

What it is: eavesdropping means secretly catching (intercepting) and watching other people's private messages without their consent. Targets include:

  • phone calls and video calls
  • instant messages and emails
  • network traffic, e.g. on unencrypted public Wi-Fi (Wi-Fi with no password protection or old security)

Why it is dangerous: the victim's network still works normally, so it is very hard to notice.

Defence: you cannot easily stop someone from capturing data, so make the data useless to them: encryption (scrambling data so only the right key can read it). Examples: HTTPS, end-to-end encrypted chat apps, WPA2/WPA3 Wi-Fi, VPN.

Exam wording: Eavesdropping refers to the unauthorised interception and monitoring of the content of other people's private communications without consent. It is difficult to detect whether the data has been intercepted. Use encryption so that intercepted data cannot be read.
cards.zh:
比喻：你在房间讲电话，有人在门外偷听，你完全不知道。

是什么：eavesdropping（窃听）就是未经同意，偷偷截取 (intercept) 和监察别人的私人通讯。对象包括：

  • 电话、视像通话
  • 即时讯息、电邮
  • 网络流量，例如没有加密的公共 Wi-Fi

为什么危险：受害人的网络照常运作，所以很难察觉资料被截取。

防范：很难阻止别人截取，所以要令截到的数据没用：encryption（加密），即把数据打乱，只有正确的 key 才能读。例如 HTTPS、端对端加密通讯软件、WPA2/WPA3、VPN。

考试写法：Eavesdropping refers to the unauthorised interception and monitoring of the content of other people's private communications without consent. It is difficult to detect whether the data has been intercepted. Use encryption so that intercepted data cannot be read.

ex.q: Why is encryption the best defence against eavesdropping, rather than trying to detect it?
ex.a:
1. Eavesdropping is hard to detect: the network looks normal.
  2. So we may never know data was captured.
  3. Encryption turns data into ciphertext (unreadable text).
  4. Even if captured, the eavesdropper cannot read it without the key.
  5. So encryption protects the data whether or not we detect the attack.
ex.az:
1. 窃听很难察觉，网络看似正常。
  2. 我们可能永远不知道被截取。
  3. 加密把数据变成密文。
  4. 没有 key，截到也看不懂。
  5. 所以不论是否察觉，加密都能保护数据。

ex.q: Mary logs in to an http:// (not https://) shop website on café Wi-Fi with no password. What is the risk and what should she do?
ex.a:
1. The Wi-Fi is open and the website uses HTTP, so data is sent in plain text.
  2. Anyone on the same Wi-Fi can capture packets and read her username and password.
  3. She should only log in to HTTPS websites, or use mobile data / a VPN.
ex.az:
1. Wi-Fi 无密码，网站用 HTTP，数据以明文传送。
  2. 同一 Wi-Fi 的人可截取封包，看到帐户和密码。
  3. 应只在 HTTPS 网站登入，或用流动数据/VPN。

ex.q: A student writes: 'Install antivirus software to prevent eavesdropping.' Is this right?
ex.a:
1. Mistake: eavesdropping happens on the network path, often on another device (e.g. a router or attacker's laptop), not as a virus on your computer.
  2. Antivirus cannot stop someone capturing packets in the air.
  3. Correct answer: encrypt the communication (HTTPS, VPN, end-to-end encryption, WPA2 Wi-Fi).
ex.az:
1. 错误：窃听发生在传输途中（例如路由器或黑客的电脑），不是你电脑上的病毒。
  2. 防毒软件不能阻止别人截取封包。
  3. 正确：加密通讯（HTTPS、VPN、端对端加密、WPA2）。

frames.en: Mary sends pw=cat123 to the server over open Wi-Fi.
frames.zh: Mary 经公开 Wi-Fi 把 pw=cat123 传给伺服器。

frames.en: The eavesdropper quietly copies the packet. Mary's connection still works, so she notices nothing.
frames.zh: 窃听者偷偷复制封包。Mary 的连线照常，她毫无察觉。

frames.en: Now the data is encrypted before it leaves Mary's device.
frames.zh: 现在数据离开 Mary 的设备前已加密。

frames.en: The eavesdropper only sees ciphertext. Only the server has the key to decrypt it.
frames.zh: 窃听者只看到密文。只有伺服器有 key 解密。

cards.en:
Analogy: a burglar who picks the lock of your house. Once inside, he can steal things, smash things, or use your house as a base.

What it is: hacking is when hackers use different methods to attack network security and get unauthorised access (entry without permission) to a computer or system.

Consequences (memorise 3):

  • Data and files may be stolen or destroyed.
  • A website's content may be changed and vandalised.
  • The computer may become a zombie computer (a computer secretly controlled by the hacker) and launch a denial-of-service (DoS) attack (flooding a website with requests so it stops working).

Losses:

EnterpriseCitizens
leaked customer data, compensation, legal liability, lost customers and reputationidentity theft, money loss

In Hong Kong it is a crime: Telecommunications Ordinance s.27A, Crimes Ordinance s.161.

Exam wording: Hacking refers to hackers' behaviour of using different methods to attack and destroy network security. Data and files stored in the computer may be stolen or destroyed; the content of a website may be changed; the computer may become a zombie computer and launch a denial-of-service attack.

Book case (Activity 5.5): an airline's system was hacked and about 9.4 million passengers' data (names, passport and ID numbers, contact details) was accessed. Enterprise losses: reputation, customers, revenue, compensation. Citizens: privacy violated; stolen card numbers used for transactions.
cards.zh:
比喻：小偷撬开你家门锁，入屋后可以偷东西、破坏东西，甚至把你家当据点。

是什么：hacking（黑客入侵）指黑客用不同方法攻击网络保安，未经授权 (unauthorised access) 进入电脑或系统。

后果（背 3 个）：

  • 资料文件被偷或被破坏。
  • 网站内容被篡改。
  • 电脑变成 zombie computer（僵尸电脑，被黑客暗中控制），去发动 denial-of-service (DoS) 攻击（大量请求令网站瘫痪）。

损失：企业——客户资料外泄、赔偿、法律责任、失去客户和声誉；市民——身份盗用、金钱损失。

在香港属刑事罪行（电讯条例 27A、刑事罪行条例 161）。

考试写法：Hacking refers to hackers' behaviour of using different methods to attack and destroy network security. Data may be stolen or destroyed; website content may be changed; the computer may become a zombie computer and launch a denial-of-service attack.

课本个案（活动 5.5）：某航空公司系统被入侵，约 940 万乘客资料（姓名、护照及身份证号码、联络资料）被存取。企业损失：声誉、客户、收入、赔偿；市民：私隐受侵犯、信用卡号被盗用。

ex.q: An airline's customer database is hacked. State one loss to the airline and one to customers.
ex.a:
1. Airline: must pay compensation / faces legal liability / loses reputation and customers.
  2. Customers: their personal data (passport no., address) is leaked, which may lead to identity theft or money loss.
ex.az:
1. 航空公司：赔偿、法律责任、失去声誉及客户。
  2. 乘客：护照号码、地址等外泄，可能被身份盗用或金钱损失。

ex.q: Tom's PC is slow and its network light flashes all night, but he isn't using it. What may have happened?
ex.a:
1. His PC may have been hacked and turned into a zombie computer.
  2. The hacker uses it to send huge numbers of requests to a target website (DoS attack).
  3. Fix: disconnect, scan with antivirus, update OS, change passwords.
ex.az:
1. 电脑可能被入侵，变成 zombie computer。
  2. 黑客用它向目标网站大量发送请求（DoS 攻击）。
  3. 处理：断网、扫毒、更新系统、改密码。

ex.q: A student writes: 'Hacking only harms the hacked computer's owner.' Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: a hacked computer can become a zombie and attack other websites (DoS).
  2. Stolen data harms the people in the data (customers), not only the owner.
  3. So hacking harms third parties too.
ex.az:
1. 错误：被入侵电脑可变成 zombie 攻击其他网站。
  2. 被盗资料伤害资料中的其他人（客户）。
  3. 所以第三方也受害。

demo.title: From hacked PC to zombie to DoS

frames.en: The hacker exploits a weak password to gain unauthorised access to PC A.
frames.zh: 黑客利用弱密码未经授权进入电脑 A。

frames.en: Files on PC A are copied or deleted.
frames.zh: 电脑 A 的文件被复制或删除。

frames.en: PC A and PC B are now zombie computers, waiting for the hacker's command.
frames.zh: 电脑 A、B 成为 zombie computer，等候黑客指令。

frames.en: All zombies flood the website with requests. Real users can't get in.
frames.zh: 所有 zombie 向网站大量发请求，真用户无法使用。

cards.en:
Analogy: instead of breaking the lock, the thief knocks and says "I'm the plumber" and you open the door yourself.

What it is: social engineering tricks people, not machines. The scammer uses your trust or your greed to make you give away secret information such as passwords or credit card numbers.

  • Because it attacks people, a firewall or antivirus cannot fully stop it: you type the password in yourself.
  • It is also a common way to spread malware (harmful software), e.g. you are tricked into opening a file.

Five types in the syllabus: baiting, quid pro quo, catfishing, pretexting, phishing (see next cards).

General defence:

  • be suspicious of unexpected requests
  • check identity through another channel (call the official number yourself)
  • never give passwords or one-time verification codes
  • HK Anti-Deception hotline: 18222

Exam wording: Social engineering refers to a scammer's behaviour of manipulating the trust between people or the victim's greed to trick the victims into disclosing confidential personal information. It is also a common method of spreading malware.
cards.zh:
比喻：小偷不撬锁，而是敲门说“我是水喉师傅”，你自己开门。

是什么：social engineering（社交工程）骗的是人不是机器。骗徒利用你的信任或贪念，令你交出密码、信用卡号码等机密资料。

  • 因为攻击的是人，防火墙和防毒软件不能完全阻止——密码是你自己输入的。
  • 亦是散播恶意软件 (malware) 的常见方法，例如骗你开启文件。

课程五种：baiting、quid pro quo、catfishing、pretexting、phishing。

防范：对意外要求保持怀疑；用另一途径核实身份（自己打官方电话）；绝不透露密码或验证码；防骗热线 18222。

考试写法：Social engineering refers to a scammer's behaviour of manipulating the trust between people or the victim's greed to trick the victims into disclosing confidential personal information. It is also a common method of spreading malware.

ex.q: Why can't antivirus software fully protect against social engineering?
ex.a:
1. Antivirus detects harmful programs.
  2. Social engineering tricks the user into giving information voluntarily, e.g. telling a password on the phone.
  3. No malware is involved, so antivirus has nothing to detect.
  4. Defence must be user awareness/education.
ex.az:
1. 防毒软件侦测的是恶意程式。
  2. 社交工程骗用户自愿交出资料（如电话里说出密码）。
  3. 没有恶意程式，防毒软件无从侦测。
  4. 要靠用户警觉和教育。

ex.q: Someone calls Mrs Chan: 'This is ABC Bank. Your account is locked. Tell me the SMS code we just sent.' What should she do?
ex.a:
1. This uses trust in a bank (social engineering).
  2. Banks never ask for verification codes.
  3. Hang up, call the bank's official number herself to check.
  4. Report to 18222 if it is a scam.
ex.az:
1. 利用对银行的信任（社交工程）。
  2. 银行从不索取验证码。
  3. 挂线，自己打银行官方电话核实。
  4. 如属骗案可致电 18222。

ex.q: A student says: 'Our company has a strong firewall, so social engineering is not a threat.' Comment.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: a firewall filters network traffic; it cannot stop an employee giving a password to a fake 'IT staff' caller.
  2. Correct: also train staff, use 2FA, set rules to verify callers.
ex.az:
1. 错误：防火墙过滤网络流量，挡不住员工把密码告诉假冒的“IT 人员”。
  2. 正确：还要培训员工、用双重认证、制定核实身份程序。

cards.en:
Analogy: baiting is cheese in a mouse trap. Quid pro quo is a stranger saying "I'll give you a free gift if you tell me your PIN".

BaitingQuid pro quo
Usesthe victim's curiositythe victim's wish for a benefit (greed)
Howleaves a USB drive / CD with malware in a public place; someone plugs it in and malware installs automaticallyoffers a service or goods in exchange for personal information ("something for something")
ExampleUSB labelled "Exam answers" left in the library"Free tech support / free gift, just give us your email and password"
Defencenever plug in unknown USB drives; hand them to staffno real service needs your password; refuse

Exam wording: Baiting: scammers exploit the victim's curiosity, e.g. leaving USB drives containing malware in public places. Quid pro quo: scammers claim to provide services or goods and ask the victim to disclose personal information in exchange.
cards.zh:
比喻：baiting 像捕鼠器上的芝士；quid pro quo 像陌生人说“告诉我密码就送你礼物”。

Baiting 诱饵Quid pro quo 交换条件
利用好奇心想得到好处（贪念）
做法在公众地方留下载有恶意软件的 USB/光碟，有人插入电脑就自动安装声称提供服务或货品，要求用个人资料交换
例子图书馆里写着“考试答案”的 USB“免费技术支援/礼物，只需电邮和密码”
防范不插来历不明的 USB，交给职员正当服务不会要密码，拒绝

考试写法：Baiting: scammers exploit the victim's curiosity, e.g. leaving USB drives containing malware in public places. Quid pro quo: scammers claim to provide services or goods and ask the victim to disclose personal information in exchange.

ex.q: A caller says 'I'm from IT support; I'll upgrade your PC for free if you give me your login password.' Which attack?
ex.a:
1. A free service (upgrade) is offered.
  2. In exchange, the victim must give information (password).
  3. So it is quid pro quo.
ex.az:
1. 提供免费服务（升级）。
  2. 作为交换要交出密码。
  3. 所以是 quid pro quo。

ex.q: Peter finds a USB drive labelled 'Staff salaries 2026' in the canteen and plugs it into the office PC. Which attack, and what may happen?
ex.a:
1. The label makes him curious: baiting.
  2. Malware on the USB may install automatically.
  3. It may steal data or let a hacker control the PC.
  4. He should give it to IT staff instead.
ex.az:
1. 标签引起好奇：baiting。
  2. USB 内恶意软件可能自动安装。
  3. 可能盗取资料或让黑客控制电脑。
  4. 应交给 IT 部门。

ex.q: A student classifies 'Click here to claim your free iPhone – enter your card number' as baiting. Right?
ex.a:
1. Mistake: baiting relies on curiosity with a bait object (USB/CD) that delivers malware.
  2. Here a gift is promised in exchange for card details.
  3. Correct answer: quid pro quo (often delivered through a phishing message).
ex.az:
1. 错误：baiting 靠好奇心和诱饵（USB/光碟）放恶意软件。
  2. 这里是承诺礼物换取信用卡资料。
  3. 正确：quid pro quo（常经钓鱼讯息发出）。

cards.en:
Analogy: catfishing is a stranger wearing someone else's face online for months. Pretexting is someone phoning and saying "Hi, it's your cousin" with a made-up story.

CatfishingPretexting
Whatuses other people's photos and personal information to create fake social media accounts, builds a relationship (often romance), then invents sad stories to ask for moneypretends to be someone else (friend, bank officer, police) to gain trust and get information or money
Timelong (weeks to years)usually short, one story
Examplea HK woman sent HK$180 million over four years to a "British engineer" she never meta "friend" on WhatsApp asks for your verification code, takes over your account and asks your contacts to buy gift cards

Signs of catfishing: refuses video calls or meeting; strange excuses; keeps asking for money; photos found elsewhere online (reverse image search).

Defence: verify by calling the real person directly; never share verification codes; never send money to people you haven't met.

Exam wording: Catfishing: scammers use others' photos and personal information to create fake social media accounts and ask for money. Pretexting: scammers pretend to be someone else to gain the victim's trust.

Book tips: catfishers make up excuses to hide who they are and refuse video calls or meetings. Pretexting example: a 'friend' says his phone is broken and asks you to forward a WhatsApp verification code — this lets the scammer take over your account. Never give verification codes to anyone; call the friend directly to check. Anti-Deception Coordination Centre hotline: 18222.
cards.zh:
比喻：catfishing 像陌生人在网上长期“戴着别人的脸”；pretexting 像有人打来说“我是你表哥”，再编个故事。

CatfishingPretexting 假托
做法盗用他人相片和资料建立假社交帐户，发展关系（多为网恋），再编可怜故事要钱冒充他人（朋友、银行职员、警察）取得信任，骗资料或钱
时间长（数周至数年）通常较短
例子港女四年汇款 1.8 亿给从未见面的“英国工程师”WhatsApp“朋友”要你的验证码，盗帐户后叫你的联络人买礼品卡

Catfishing 迹象：拒绝视像或见面、借口古怪、不断要钱、相片可在网上找到（以图搜图）。

防范：直接致电本人核实；绝不分享验证码；不汇钱给未见过面的人。

考试写法：Catfishing: scammers use others' photos and personal information to create fake social media accounts and ask for money. Pretexting: scammers pretend to be someone else to gain the victim's trust.

课本提示：交友骗徒会找借口隐藏身份、拒绝视像通话或见面。假托例子：「朋友」说手机坏了，叫你转发 WhatsApp 验证码，骗徒就能夺取你的帐户。永不把验证码给别人，直接打电话给朋友核实。防骗易热线 18222。

ex.q: Suggest TWO ways to identify catfishing.
ex.a:
1. The person always refuses video calls or meeting in person.
  2. They keep asking for money with sad or urgent stories.
  3. (Also: a reverse image search shows their photos belong to someone else.)
ex.az:
1. 对方总是拒绝视像或见面。
  2. 不断以可怜或紧急故事要钱。
  3. （亦可：以图搜图发现相片属于别人。）

ex.q: Amy gets a WhatsApp: 'Hi it's Ken, new number! I sent you a code by mistake, can you forward it?' Which attack and what should she do?
ex.a:
1. The scammer pretends to be her friend Ken: pretexting.
  2. The code is a login code; forwarding it lets the scammer take over her account.
  3. She should call Ken's old number to check and never forward codes.
ex.az:
1. 冒充朋友 Ken：pretexting。
  2. 那是登入验证码，转发会令帐户被盗。
  3. 应打 Ken 旧号码核实，绝不转发验证码。

ex.q: A student says catfishing and pretexting are the same because both pretend to be someone. Explain the difference.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: they are not identical.
  2. Catfishing builds a fake social media identity using someone's photos and a long-term relationship before asking for money.
  3. Pretexting is pretending to be a specific trusted person/role with a made-up reason, usually in one short contact.
ex.az:
1. 错误：两者不同。
  2. Catfishing 用他人相片建假社交身份，长期经营关系才要钱。
  3. Pretexting 是以借口冒充某个可信的人/身份，通常一次短接触。

ex.q: A 'friend' on WhatsApp asks you to send the 6-digit code you just received. What should you do?
ex.a: Do not send it. Call the friend directly to verify; the code would let a scammer log in to your account.
ex.az: 不要发，直接打电话核实；验证码会让骗徒登入你的帐户。

cards.en:
Analogy: fishing with a fake worm. The fake email or SMS is the bait; the fake website is the hook.

What it is: scammers forge official websites and send emails/SMS that trick victims into visiting the fake site and typing in personal information (login names, passwords, credit card numbers).

  • Phishing website: a fake website made to look like a real one, e.g. a fake Hongkong Post page asking you to pay a parcel fee.
  • QR code phishing: a QR code that opens a phishing website.

How to spot it:

  • sender address or URL slightly misspelt / not the official domain (e.g. hongk0ngpost-pay.com)
  • urgent or threatening tone ("within 24 hours")
  • asks for passwords or card details
  • generic greeting ("Dear customer")
  • link text differs from the real address

Defence: don't click links in suspicious messages; type the official URL yourself; check HTTPS and the certificate; report to the organisation.

Exam wording: Phishing refers to scammers' behaviour of forging official websites and sending messages to deceive victims into visiting fake websites and entering personal information.

Book Activity 5.9, signs of a phishing email: suspicious or public sender address (e.g. a bank using @gmail.com); threatening subject; general greeting ('Hello'); spelling/grammar mistakes; requests personal data; no secure channel (http, not https); urgent deadline. A real email: official domain, uses your name and partial account number, does not ask for information by email. TIP: a website with gov as the top-level domain is an official government website. Misconception: 'https' means the connection is encrypted, not that the site is genuine.
cards.zh:
比喻：用假鱼饵钓鱼。假电邮/短讯是饵，假网站是钩。

是什么：骗徒伪造官方网站，发电邮/短讯骗受害人进入假网站并输入个人资料（帐户、密码、信用卡号码）。

  • Phishing website：仿真假网站，如假香港邮政要求缴包裹费。
  • QR code phishing：扫 QR code 后打开钓鱼网站。

识别：寄件地址/网址拼错或非官方域名（如 hongk0ngpost-pay.com）；语气紧急或威吓；索取密码或信用卡；称呼笼统；连结文字与实际网址不同。

防范：不按可疑连结；自己输入官方网址；检查 HTTPS 和证书；向机构举报。

考试写法：Phishing refers to scammers' behaviour of forging official websites and sending messages to deceive victims into visiting fake websites and entering personal information.

课本活动 5.9，钓鱼邮件特征：可疑或公共邮箱地址（银行用 @gmail.com）；威胁性标题；泛称问候；拼字文法错误；索取个人资料；没有安全通道（http）；制造紧急气氛。真邮件：官方域名、称呼你名字和部分帐号、不会用电邮索取资料。TIP：顶级域名是 gov 的是政府官方网站。误解：https 只代表连线加密，不代表网站真确。

ex.q: An email from 'service@hongk0ngpost-pay.com' says your parcel is held; pay HK$12 at the link within 24 hours. Give three phishing signs.
ex.a:
1. The domain is not official and uses a zero instead of 'o' (hongk0ngpost).
  2. Urgent tone: 'within 24 hours'.
  3. Asks for payment/card details through a link.
ex.az:
1. 域名非官方，用 0 代替 o。
  2. 语气紧急：“24 小时内”。
  3. 经连结索取付款/信用卡资料。

ex.q: A link shows the text 'https://www.abcbank.com.hk' but when you hover over it the status bar shows 'http://abcbank-login.xyz'. What does this mean?
ex.a:
1. The displayed text is not the real destination.
  2. The real address is a different, unofficial domain without HTTPS.
  3. This is a phishing link; don't click; type the bank's URL yourself.
ex.az:
1. 显示文字不是真正目的地。
  2. 实际网址是另一个非官方域名，且非 HTTPS。
  3. 属钓鱼连结；不要按，自己输入银行网址。

ex.q: A student says: 'The site shows a padlock (HTTPS), so it can't be phishing.' Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: HTTPS only means the connection is encrypted.
  2. Scammers can get a certificate for their own fake domain too.
  3. You must also check the domain name is the official one.
ex.az:
1. 错误：HTTPS 只代表连线加密。
  2. 骗徒也可为自己的假域名申请证书。
  3. 还要检查域名是否官方。

ex.q: An email from Sky Bank <sky@gmail.com> says your account is suspended and to verify at an http link within 2 days. List three warning signs.
ex.a:
1. Public Gmail address, not the bank's domain.
2. Threatening, urgent deadline.
3. Asks for personal data via a non-HTTPS link.
ex.az: 公共邮箱、威胁紧急、经非 https 连结索取资料。

frames.en: The scammer sends an SMS: 'Parcel held. Pay HK$12 within 24h: hongk0ngpost-pay.com'.
frames.zh: 骗徒发短讯：“包裹被扣，24 小时内缴 HK$12”。

frames.en: The victim clicks the link and lands on the fake website, which looks exactly like the real one.
frames.zh: 受害人按连结，进入与真网站一模一样的假网站。

frames.en: The victim types card number and CVV. The data goes to the scammer, not the post office.
frames.zh: 受害人输入信用卡号码及 CVV，资料传给骗徒而非邮政。

frames.en: Instead: ignore the link, type the official URL yourself, and check the parcel there.
frames.zh: 正确做法：不理连结，自行输入官方网址查询。

cards.en:
Analogy: junk flyers stuffed in your mailbox every day, but digital and in thousands.

What it is: spamming is sending a large number of unwanted messages by SMS or email without the recipient's consent.

Problems:

  • wastes time, storage and bandwidth
  • can be fraudulent: phishing links, malware attachments

Law in HK: commercial electronic messages are controlled by the Unsolicited Electronic Messages Ordinance (Cap. 593). Recipients can refuse (unsubscribe), and senders must honour the request. (Book example: a tutoring agency was investigated for unsolicited messages.)

Defence: spam filter; don't reply or click (replying confirms your address is active); unsubscribe from legitimate senders; report.

Exam wording: Spamming of electronic messages refers to the behaviour of sending a large number of redundant messages through SMS or emails without the recipient's consent.

Book details: spam can fill the mailbox quota so you cannot send or receive mail (or must pay to upgrade). Clicking a link in spam can infect your computer, lead to a phishing site, and tell the sender your address is active (more spam). UEMO case: commercial messages must have accurate sender information and must not go to numbers on the Do-not-call Registers.
cards.zh:
比喻：每天塞满信箱的宣传单张，只不过是电子版、成千上万。

是什么：spamming（滥发讯息）指未经收件人同意，经短讯或电邮大量发送多余讯息。

问题：浪费时间、储存空间、频宽；可能带诈骗（钓鱼连结、恶意附件）。

香港法例：商业电子讯息受《非应邀电子讯息条例》(Cap. 593) 规管：收件人可拒收（退订），发送者必须遵从。（书例：补习中介因滥发讯息被调查。）

防范：垃圾邮件过滤；不回复、不按连结（回复会证实地址有效）；向正当发送者退订；举报。

考试写法：Spamming of electronic messages refers to the behaviour of sending a large number of redundant messages through SMS or emails without the recipient's consent.

课本补充：垃圾讯息可塞满邮箱容量，令你不能收发（或要付费升级）。按垃圾邮件的连结可能中毒、被带到钓鱼网站，并让发送者知道你的地址有效（更多垃圾邮件）。《非应邀电子讯息条例》：商业讯息必须有准确发送者资料，不可发给已登记拒收讯息登记册的号码。

ex.q: A shop keeps sending promotional SMS after Lily replied 'unsubscribe'. Which law may be violated?
ex.a:
1. The SMS are commercial electronic messages.
  2. Lily has refused them.
  3. Continuing breaks the Unsolicited Electronic Messages Ordinance (Cap. 593).
ex.az:
1. 属商业电子讯息。
  2. Lily 已拒收。
  3. 继续发送违反 Cap. 593。

ex.q: Give two harms of spam emails to a company.
ex.a:
1. Staff waste time deleting them; mailbox storage and bandwidth are used up.
  2. Some carry phishing links or malware, risking a data breach.
ex.az:
1. 员工浪费时间删除；占用储存与频宽。
  2. 部分带钓鱼连结或恶意软件，有资料外泄风险。

ex.q: A student advises: 'Reply STOP to every spam email you get.' Is this always good?
ex.a:
1. Mistake: for unknown/fraudulent spammers, replying confirms your address is active, so you get more spam.
  2. Only unsubscribe from legitimate companies you know.
  3. For unknown spam: don't reply, mark as spam, delete.
ex.az:
1. 错误：对不明/诈骗发送者，回复会证实地址有效，收到更多。
  2. 只向认识的正当公司退订。
  3. 不明 spam：不回复、标记为垃圾、删除。

ex.q: Yuki clicked a link in a fake bank email but typed nothing. Give two possible threats. (DSE 2016 1B)
ex.a:
1. Malicious code may infect her computer.
2. She may be sent to a phishing site.
3. The sender learns her address is active and sends more spam.
ex.az: 可能中毒；被带到钓鱼网站；对方知道地址有效会发更多垃圾邮件。

cards.en:
Analogy: each post is one jigsaw piece. One piece says little. Put enough together and a stranger sees your whole picture: name, school, home, routine.

What it is: people show personal information on public platforms to make friends. Showing too much (phone number, address…) may lead to identity theft (someone pretending to be you, e.g. opening accounts in your name).

Personal information = information that can identify a person: name, date of birth, phone, address, photo, ID number, school. The easier it identifies you, the more sensitive it is.

Consequences: identity theft, cyber bullying, doxing (publishing someone's private details), stalking, money loss, stress.

Defence: set accounts to private; share as little as possible; turn off location tags; never post ID cards or tickets with barcodes.

Exam wording: Disclosure of too much personal information on the Internet, such as phone numbers and addresses, may lead to identity theft.
cards.zh:
比喻：每个帖子是一块拼图。一块没什么，拼多了陌生人就看到你的全貌：名字、学校、住址、作息。

是什么：不少人在公开平台展示个人资料结识朋友。披露过多（电话、地址等）可能导致 identity theft（身份盗用），即别人冒充你，例如用你的名义开户。

个人资料＝可识别个人的资料：姓名、出生日期、电话、地址、相片、身份证号码、学校。愈易识别愈敏感。

后果：身份盗用、网络欺凌、起底 (doxing)、跟踪、金钱损失、精神压力。

防范：帐户设私人；尽量少分享；关闭定位标签；不贴身份证或有条码的票。

考试写法：Disclosure of too much personal information on the Internet, such as phone numbers and addresses, may lead to identity theft.

ex.q: Tom posts his full name, birthday, school and a photo of his HKID card. Explain the risk.
ex.a:
1. Name + birthday + HKID number are enough to impersonate him.
  2. A criminal could open accounts or apply for loans in his name: identity theft.
  3. School info also lets strangers find him (stalking).
  4. He should delete the post and set the account to private.
ex.az:
1. 姓名＋生日＋身份证号码足以冒充他。
  2. 罪犯可用他名义开户或借贷：身份盗用。
  3. 学校资料令陌生人找到他（跟踪）。
  4. 应删帖并设私人帐户。

ex.q: Ivy never posts her address, but posts daily photos in her uniform with location tags at the same bus stop. Is she safe?
ex.a:
1. Small details combine: uniform → school; tag → bus stop; time → routine.
  2. A stranger could work out where she goes every day.
  3. She should turn off location tags and avoid showing the school badge.
ex.az:
1. 零碎资料可组合：校服→学校；定位→车站；时间→作息。
  2. 陌生人可推断她每天行踪。
  3. 应关闭定位，避免露出校徽。

ex.q: A student writes: 'Only my HKID number is personal information; my photo is not.' Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: personal information is any information that can identify a person.
  2. A photo of your face can identify you, so it is personal information.
  3. Name, phone, address, school, birthday also count.
ex.az:
1. 错误：个人资料是任何可识别个人的资料。
  2. 样貌相片可识别你，所以也是。
  3. 姓名、电话、地址、学校、生日都算。

cards.en:
Analogy: a bakery that wants your HKID card and salary slip before selling you one bun.

What it is: many online registrations ask for personal information that has nothing to do with the service, e.g. a free game app asking for HKID number and home address.

Risk: the information may be accessed or transferred to a third party for commercial purposes, or even leaked. The more data a company stores, the more can be lost in a hack.

Rule: under the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance, data users should only collect data that is necessary and not excessive for the purpose.

What users should do: check which fields are compulsory; read the privacy policy; refuse to give data that is not needed; choose another service.

Exam wording: Many online system registrations require users to provide personal information that has nothing to do with the nature of the service. Personal information may be accessed or transferred to a third party for commercial purposes, or even leaked.
cards.zh:
比喻：买一个面包，面包店却要你的身份证和粮单。

是什么：很多网上登记要求提供与服务无关的个人资料，例如免费游戏要身份证号码和住址。

风险：资料可能被转给第三方作商业用途，甚至外泄。储存愈多，被入侵时损失愈大。

规则：根据《个人资料（私隐）条例》，只应收集必需而不过度的资料。

用户应：查看哪些必填；读私隐政策；拒绝不必要资料；改用其他服务。

考试写法：Many online system registrations require users to provide personal information that has nothing to do with the nature of the service. Personal information may be accessed or transferred to a third party for commercial purposes, or even leaked.

ex.q: A cinema app requires HKID number, monthly income and home address to buy a ticket. Comment.
ex.a:
1. Buying a ticket needs at most a contact (email/phone) and payment.
  2. HKID, income and address are not related to the service: over-collection.
  3. Risk: sold to third parties or leaked.
  4. Against the PDPO principle of collecting only necessary data.
ex.az:
1. 买票最多需联络方法和付款。
  2. 身份证、收入、地址与服务无关：过度收集。
  3. 风险：被卖给第三方或外泄。
  4. 违反私隐条例只收集必需资料的原则。

ex.q: Decide which fields are reasonable for an online library book-reservation form: name, library card no., phone, blood type, income.
ex.a:
1. Name, library card no.: needed to identify the borrower ✔
  2. Phone: to notify when the book arrives ✔
  3. Blood type, income: unrelated ✘ (over-collection)
ex.az:
1. 姓名、借书证号码：识别借书人 ✔
  2. 电话：通知取书 ✔
  3. 血型、收入：无关 ✘

ex.q: A student says: 'If a field is on the form, I must fill it in.' Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: many fields are optional (no * mark).
  2. Leave optional fields empty and give only what is necessary.
  3. If unrelated data is compulsory, you may refuse and use another service.
ex.az:
1. 错误：很多栏位是选填（无 * 号）。
  2. 选填可留空，只给必需资料。
  3. 若无关资料必填，可拒绝改用其他服务。

cards.en:
Analogy: walking through a shopping mall leaves footprints. Anonymity means cleaning your footprints and, if needed, walking behind someone else so cameras don't see you.

Why: to protect privacy we keep an anonymous identity so our activities are not tracked and leave no traces.

Four methods in the book:

  1. Clear browsing history and cookies
  2. Turn off the autofill function
  3. Use private browsing
  4. Use a proxy server (or VPN) to hide the IP address

Key point: even if you type no personal data, every data packet contains the sender's and recipient's IP addresses (IP address = the number that identifies your device on the Internet). So your ISP, websites or a network administrator can still record your activity. Methods 1–3 only clean your own device; only method 4 hides your IP.

MethodHides from next user of the device?Hides IP from website?
Clear history/cookies✔✘
Autofill off✔✘
Private browsing✔✘
Proxy / VPN✘✔

Exam wording: Clear browsing history and cookies; turn off the autofill function; use private browsing; use a proxy server to hide the IP address.
cards.zh:
比喻：逛商场会留下脚印。匿名就是清走脚印，必要时躲在别人身后，令镜头拍不到你。

为什么：为保护私隐，应保持匿名身份，避免活动被追踪或留下痕迹。

书中四法：①清除浏览纪录及 cookies ②关闭 autofill ③使用私密浏览 ④使用 proxy server（或 VPN）隐藏 IP。

重点：即使不输入个人资料，每个封包都有寄件及收件 IP 地址（IP 地址＝在互联网识别设备的号码），ISP、网站、网管仍可记录你的活动。①–③只清理自己设备；只有④能隐藏 IP。

方法对下一位用户隐藏？对网站隐藏 IP？
清纪录/cookies✔✘
关 autofill✔✘
私密浏览✔✘
Proxy/VPN✘✔

考试写法：Clear browsing history and cookies; turn off the autofill function; use private browsing; use a proxy server to hide the IP address.

ex.q: After using a library computer to check email, what should Amy do to protect privacy?
ex.a:
1. Log out of her email account.
  2. Clear browsing history and cookies.
  3. Make sure autofill did not save her password (or use private browsing next time).
ex.az:
1. 登出电邮。
  2. 清除浏览纪录及 cookies。
  3. 确认 autofill 没储存密码（下次用私密浏览）。

ex.q: Ken wants a website not to know his real IP address. Which of the four methods works?
ex.a:
1. Clearing history, autofill off and private browsing only affect his own device.
  2. The website still sees the IP in the packets.
  3. Only a proxy server (or VPN) replaces his IP with the proxy's.
ex.az:
1. 清纪录、关 autofill、私密浏览只影响自己设备。
  2. 网站仍从封包看到 IP。
  3. 只有 proxy server（或 VPN）能以 proxy 的 IP 代替。

ex.q: A student writes: 'If I never type my name online, I am completely anonymous.' Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: every packet carries your IP address.
  2. The ISP, websites and network admin can link activity to that IP and to you.
  3. To hide the IP, use a proxy server or VPN.
ex.az:
1. 错误：每个封包都带有你的 IP 地址。
  2. ISP、网站、网管可把活动连到该 IP 和你。
  3. 要隐藏 IP 须用 proxy 或 VPN。

cards.en:
Analogy: a cloakroom ticket. The website gives your browser a small ticket; next time you show it, the site remembers who you are and what you left.

What it is: a cookie is a small piece of data a website stores on your device to record what you did.

Cookies record:

  • user preferences and browsing behaviour, e.g. items in a shopping cart, viewed products
  • login authentication result, so you stay logged in
  • settings like preferred language

They improve user experience but may infringe online privacy.

First-party cookiesThird-party cookies
made by the website you are visitingmade by other websites (e.g. an ad company whose ad is on the page)
cart, login, languagetrack you across websites to personalise ads

Many browsers are gradually blocking third-party cookies; you can also block cookies in settings. Clear cookies after using a public computer.

Exam wording: When a user browses a website, the website generates a cookie to store information on the device to record the user's operations, such as user preferences, browsing behaviour and login authentication results. Third-party cookies track user activity across websites.

Book enrichment: first-party cookies come from the site you are visiting; third-party cookies come from other sites and track you across websites to personalise ads (search a product, then see its ads on social media). Many browsers are phasing out third-party cookies.
cards.zh:
比喻：衣帽间的取物票。网站给浏览器一张小票，下次出示，网站就记得你是谁、留下了什么。

是什么：cookie 是网站储存在你设备上的小段数据，记录你的操作。

记录：偏好和浏览行为（购物车、看过的产品）；登入认证结果（保持登入）；语言等设定。

改善体验，但可能侵犯私隐。

First-partyThird-party
由正在浏览的网站产生由其他网站产生（如页面上广告公司）
购物车、登入、语言跨网站追踪以投放个人化广告

浏览器正逐步封锁第三方 cookies，亦可在设定封锁。用公共电脑后要清除。

考试写法：When a user browses a website, the website generates a cookie to store information on the device to record the user's operations, such as user preferences, browsing behaviour and login authentication results. Third-party cookies track user activity across websites.

课本增润：第一方 cookie 来自正在浏览的网站；第三方 cookie 来自其他网站，会跨网站追踪你以投放个人化广告。很多浏览器正逐步禁止第三方 cookie。

ex.q: Why does Ben see ads for running shoes on social media after searching shoes on an online shop?
ex.a:
1. The shop page contains an ad company's code.
  2. It sets a third-party cookie recording 'interested in running shoes'.
  3. The same ad company's code on the social media site reads that cookie.
  4. So it shows him personalised shoe ads.
ex.az:
1. 网店页面内有广告公司的程式。
  2. 它设下 third-party cookie，记录“对跑鞋有兴趣”。
  3. 社交网站上同一广告公司的程式读取该 cookie。
  4. 于是显示个人化跑鞋广告。

ex.q: Lucy closes the shop tab and reopens it the next day; her cart still has 2 items and she is still logged in. Explain.
ex.a:
1. The shop stored first-party cookies on her device.
  2. One records the cart items; one records the login authentication result.
  3. On return, the browser sends the cookies, so the site restores both.
ex.az:
1. 网店在她设备储存 first-party cookies。
  2. 一个记购物车，一个记登入结果。
  3. 再访时浏览器送回 cookies，网站据此还原。

ex.q: A student writes: 'Cookies are viruses that steal files from your computer.' Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: cookies are small data files, not programs; they cannot run or read your files.
  2. The privacy risk is tracking: they record your behaviour (especially third-party cookies).
  3. On a public PC, others could use your login cookie, so clear cookies.
ex.az:
1. 错误：cookies 是小数据文件，不是程式，不能执行或读取你的文件。
  2. 私隐风险在于追踪行为（尤其第三方）。
  3. 公共电脑上别人可用你的登入 cookie，所以要清除。

ex.q: Josh reads about Italian food on one site and then sees Italian restaurant ads on other sites. Why, and how can he reduce it?
ex.a: Third-party cookies track him across sites to personalise ads. Block third-party cookies / clear cookies / use private browsing.
ex.az: 第三方 cookie 跨网站追踪；可封锁第三方 cookie、清除 cookie、用私密浏览。

frames.en: Ben visits shop.com. The shop sets a first-party cookie cart=shoes in his browser.
frames.zh: Ben 浏览 shop.com，网店设下 first-party cookie cart=shoes。

frames.en: An ad on shop.com comes from ads.com. ads.com sets a third-party cookie id=777, likes=shoes.
frames.zh: shop.com 上的广告来自 ads.com，它设下 third-party cookie id=777, likes=shoes。

frames.en: Later Ben opens social.com, which also shows ads.com ads. The browser sends the ads.com cookie back to ads.com.
frames.zh: 之后 Ben 打开 social.com，上面也有 ads.com 广告，浏览器把 ads.com cookie 送回。

frames.en: ads.com recognises id 777 and shows running-shoe ads: tracking across websites.
frames.zh: ads.com 认出 id 777，显示跑鞋广告：跨网站追踪。

frames.en: After clearing cookies (or blocking third-party cookies), ads.com no longer recognises him.
frames.zh: 清除 cookies（或封锁第三方）后，ads.com 不再认得他。

cards.en:
Analogy: autofill is a notebook the browser keeps of everything you typed. Private browsing is a whiteboard that is wiped when you leave.

Autofill: the browser stores account names, passwords, payment methods and addresses, and fills them in next time.

  • convenient on your own device
  • very dangerous on a public computer: the next user can get your data. Turn it off or use private browsing.

Private browsing (Incognito window): does not leave browsing history, cookies and input data on the device. When all private windows close, their cookies are deleted.

Limits of private browsing:

  • it does not hide your IP address: ISP, websites and network admins can still see your activity
  • downloaded files and bookmarks you make stay on the device

Fun fact from the book: booking sites can't use your cookies to raise prices of things you viewed many times.

Exam wording: Private browsing does not leave browsing history, cookies and input data on the device, but it does not hide the IP address. Turn off autofill on public computers.

Book misconceptions: browsers can block web pages from using cookies; after you close all incognito windows, their cookies are deleted immediately. Enrichment: booking flights or hotels in incognito may show lower prices, because the site cannot use cookies to see you viewed the item many times.
cards.zh:
比喻：autofill 像浏览器替你记下所有输入的笔记簿；私密浏览像离开时会被抹净的白板。

Autofill：浏览器储存帐户、密码、付款方式、地址，下次自动填入。自己设备方便；公共电脑非常危险，下一位用户可取得资料——应关闭或用私密浏览。

私密浏览 (Incognito)：不在设备留下浏览纪录、cookies 及输入资料；关闭所有私密视窗后 cookies 删除。

限制：不隐藏 IP，ISP、网站、网管仍看到活动；下载的文件和书签会保留。

考试写法：Private browsing does not leave browsing history, cookies and input data on the device, but it does not hide the IP address. Turn off autofill on public computers.

课本澄清误解：浏览器可以阻止网页使用 cookie；关闭所有无痕视窗后，其 cookie 会立即删除。增润：用无痕模式订机票酒店可能更便宜，因网站不能凭 cookie 知道你看过多次。

ex.q: Is Tom anonymous to his school network admin when using Incognito mode? Explain.
ex.a:
1. No.
  2. Incognito only stops history/cookies being saved on the device.
  3. Packets still carry his device's IP address through the school network.
  4. The admin can log which sites that IP visited.
ex.az:
1. 不是。
  2. Incognito 只是不在设备储存纪录/cookies。
  3. 封包经学校网络时仍带他的 IP。
  4. 网管可记录该 IP 访问了哪些网站。

ex.q: At an internet café, the login box already shows someone else's email and a saved password. What went wrong, and what should the café do?
ex.a:
1. Autofill saved the previous user's details.
  2. Anyone can now log in to that account.
  3. The café should turn off autofill / password saving, or force private browsing and clear data after each session.
ex.az:
1. Autofill 储存了上一位用户资料。
  2. 任何人都可登入该帐户。
  3. 网吧应关闭 autofill，或强制私密浏览并每次清除资料。

ex.q: A student says: 'I downloaded a file in Incognito, so it disappears when I close the window.' Right?
ex.a:
1. Mistake: private browsing deletes history, cookies and form data only.
  2. Downloaded files and bookmarks stay on the device.
  3. Delete the file manually on a shared computer.
ex.az:
1. 错误：私密浏览只删除纪录、cookies 和表格资料。
  2. 下载的文件和书签会保留。
  3. 在共用电脑上要手动删除。

cards.en:
Analogy: asking a friend to buy something for you. The shop sees your friend, not you.

What it is: a proxy server is a middle computer between you and the website. Your packets go to the proxy first; the proxy sends them on.

  • The website only records the proxy's IP address, not yours → better privacy.
  • Similar role to a VPN, but the connection to the proxy is not encrypted (a VPN is).

Other functions:

  • Filtering: all packets pass through it, so it can block specific websites (schools, companies).
  • Buffer (cache): stores pages already visited, so loading the same page again is faster.
Proxy serverVPN
Hides IP✔✔
Encrypts connection✘✔

Exam wording: A proxy server establishes an intermediate connection point between the user and the website, hiding the user's IP address. The website can only record the IP address of the proxy server. Unlike a VPN, the connection is not encrypted. A proxy can also filter web pages and use a buffer to load pages faster.

Book Fig. 5.23: a proxy server and a VPN both hide your IP, but the connection to a proxy is not encrypted. A proxy also has a buffer/cache: a page visited again is fetched from the cache, so it loads faster. It does not increase the Internet connection's bandwidth (DSE 2014 1A Q26).
cards.zh:
比喻：托朋友替你买东西，店家只见到你朋友，见不到你。

是什么：proxy server 是你和网站之间的中介电脑。封包先到 proxy，再由它转发。

  • 网站只记录 proxy 的 IP，不是你的 → 私隐较好。
  • 作用似 VPN，但连到 proxy 的连线没有加密（VPN 有）。

其他功能：过滤——可封锁指定网站（学校、公司）；缓冲 (cache)——暂存浏览过的网页，再浏览更快。

ProxyVPN
隐藏 IP✔✔
加密✘✔

考试写法：A proxy server establishes an intermediate connection point between the user and the website, hiding the user's IP address. The website can only record the IP address of the proxy server. Unlike a VPN, the connection is not encrypted. A proxy can also filter web pages and use a buffer to load pages faster.

课本图 5.23：代理伺服器和 VPN 都能隐藏 IP，但连去代理的线路没有加密。代理有缓冲／快取，再看同一网页时直接从快取取出，较快。它不会增加频宽。

ex.q: Compare proxy server and VPN in two aspects.
ex.a:
1. Both hide the user's IP address from the website.
  2. A VPN encrypts the connection; a proxy does not.
ex.az:
1. 两者都对网站隐藏用户 IP。
  2. VPN 加密连线；proxy 不加密。

ex.q: A school routes all student traffic through a proxy. Give two benefits to the school.
ex.a:
1. It can filter and block unsuitable websites (e.g. gaming sites).
  2. Its cache stores popular pages, so when many students open the same page it loads faster and saves bandwidth.
ex.az:
1. 可过滤并封锁不适合的网站。
  2. 缓冲暂存热门网页，多人打开同一页更快、省频宽。

ex.q: A student says: 'I use a proxy server on public Wi-Fi, so nobody can read my data.' Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: a proxy hides your IP from the website but does not encrypt the connection.
  2. People on the same Wi-Fi can still eavesdrop on unencrypted data.
  3. Use a VPN or HTTPS for encryption.
ex.az:
1. 错误：proxy 对网站隐藏 IP，但不加密。
  2. 同一 Wi-Fi 的人仍可窃听未加密数据。
  3. 要加密应用 VPN 或 HTTPS。

demo.title: A request through a proxy server

frames.en: Your PC (IP 203.0.113.5) asks news.com directly. news.com logs 203.0.113.5.
frames.zh: 你的电脑 (IP 203.0.113.5) 直接请求 news.com，网站记下你的 IP。

frames.en: With a proxy, your request goes to the proxy first. Note: this link is NOT encrypted.
frames.zh: 用 proxy 时，请求先送到 proxy。注意：这段连线没有加密。

frames.en: The proxy checks its block list. news.com is allowed (a blocked site would be stopped here).
frames.zh: Proxy 检查封锁名单，news.com 获准（被封锁的网站会在此被拦）。

frames.en: The proxy sends the request with ITS OWN IP. news.com only logs 198.51.100.9.
frames.zh: Proxy 用自己的 IP 转发，news.com 只记录 198.51.100.9。

frames.en: The page returns via the proxy, which keeps a copy in its buffer. Next time it is served from cache: faster.
frames.zh: 网页经 proxy 传回，proxy 在缓冲留副本；下次直接从 cache 提供，更快。

cards.en:
Analogy: a combination lock. A 3-digit lock has 1,000 combinations; a thief tries them all in minutes. More positions and more symbols per position = far more combinations.

Why: a password verifies who you are. A strong password stops hackers cracking it easily, e.g. by brute force (trying every combination) or a dictionary attack (trying common words).

Book's rules:

  • at least 8 characters
  • a mix with at least 1 number, 1 uppercase letter, 1 lowercase letter and 1 special character
  • no personal information (birthday, phone number)
  • not too simple (e.g. 123456)
  • no common words (e.g. password)

Why it works (maths):

Password typeCombinations
6 digits106 = 1,000,000
8 lowercase letters268 ≈ 2.1×1011
8 chars from 94 printable symbols948 ≈ 6.1×1015

Try the checker below. Note a program can't know your birthday, so "no personal info" still needs your own judgement.

Exam wording: Use at least 8 characters with a mixed combination of numbers, uppercase letters, lowercase letters and special characters; do not use personal information, simple passwords or common words.

Book TIP, the sentence trick: take the first letter of each word of a sentence you remember: 'my first time winning the Championship was in 2021' → mftwtCwi2021. Easy to remember, hard to guess. Enrichment: the worst passwords of 2020 included 123456, 123456789, picture1, password, 12345678, 111111 — most cracked in under 1 second.
cards.zh:
比喻：密码锁。3 位数字锁只有 1,000 个组合，几分钟就试完；位数愈多、每位符号愈多，组合多得多。

为什么：密码用来认证身份。强密码令黑客难以破解，例如 brute force（暴力破解，逐个组合试）或 dictionary attack（字典攻击，试常见字）。

书中规则：至少 8 个字元；混合至少 1 个数字、1 个大写、1 个小写、1 个特殊符号；不用个人资料（生日、电话）；不用太简单的（123456）；不用常见字（password）。

数学：6 位数字 106=1,000,000；8 个小写 268≈2.1×1011；8 位、94 种字元 948≈6.1×1015。

试试下面的检查程式。程式不会知道你的生日，所以“不用个人资料”仍要自己判断。

考试写法：Use at least 8 characters with a mixed combination of numbers, uppercase letters, lowercase letters and special characters; do not use personal information, simple passwords or common words.

课本 TIP，句子法：取一句你记得的英文句子每个字的首字母：“my first time winning the Championship was in 2021” → mftwtCwi2021，易记难猜。增润：2020 最差密码有 123456、123456789、picture1、password、12345678、111111，多数不到 1 秒就被破解。

ex.q: Check each password: (a) Tom20080315 (b) password1! (c) G7#kq!2Lm
ex.a:
1. (a) Weak: no special character, and it is a name + birthday (personal information).
  2. (b) Weak: no uppercase letter; contains the common word 'password'.
  3. (c) Strong: 9 characters with digit, upper, lower and special characters, no word or personal info.
ex.az:
1. (a) 弱：没有特殊符号，且是名字＋生日。
  2. (b) 弱：没有大写；含常见字 password。
  3. (c) 强：9 位，含数字、大小写、特殊符号，无常见字或个人资料。

ex.q: How many combinations does a 4-digit PIN have, compared with a 4-character password using 94 symbols?
ex.a:
1. PIN: each position has 10 choices → 104 = 10,000.
  2. Password: 944 = 78,074,896.
  3. So more symbol types make brute force much slower (about 7,800 times more combinations here).
ex.az:
1. PIN：每位 10 种 → 104=10,000。
  2. 密码：944=78,074,896。
  3. 符号种类多，暴力破解慢得多（约 7,800 倍）。

ex.q: A student thinks 'P@ssw0rd' is strong because it has upper, lower, number and symbol. Comment.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: it meets the mix rule but is just the common word 'password' with simple swaps (a→@, o→0).
  2. Dictionary attacks already try these swaps, so it is cracked quickly.
  3. Use an unpredictable mix or a long passphrase of unrelated words with symbols.
ex.az:
1. 错误：虽符合混合规则，但只是常见字 password 简单替换（a→@、o→0）。
  2. 字典攻击会试这些替换，很快被破。
  3. 应用难以预测的组合或较长的无关词组加符号。

ex.q: Make a password from 'I joined the HKOI team in 2026!' using the book's trick.
ex.a: Take first letters, keep capitals, digits and the symbol: IjtHtti2026!
ex.az: 取首字母并保留大写、数字和符号：IjtHtti2026!

notes.t: Import the string module (gives string.punctuation = all special characters).
notes.tz: 导入 string 模块（提供 string.punctuation 特殊符号）。

notes.t: Define a function check that takes one password pw.
notes.tz: 定义函数 check，参数为密码 pw。

notes.t: Start an empty list to collect the rules that fail.
notes.tz: 建立空列表记录不合格的规则。

notes.t: Rule 2: any() is False if no character is a digit.
notes.tz: 规则 2：没有任何数字时 any() 为 False。

notes.t: Rule 3: check for at least one uppercase letter.
notes.tz: 规则 3：至少一个大写字母。

notes.t: Rule 4: check for at least one lowercase letter.
notes.tz: 规则 4：至少一个小写字母。

notes.t: Rule 5: check for at least one special character.
notes.tz: 规则 5：至少一个特殊符号。

notes.t: Rule 6: contains the common word 'password' or is a too-simple password.
notes.tz: 规则 6：含常见字 password 或太简单。

notes.t: Run the checks on this password.
Print STRONG if no problems, else WEAK and the reasons joined by commas.
notes.tz: 没问题印 STRONG，否则印 WEAK 及原因。

code.out:
Tom20080315 -> WEAK: no special character
password1! -> WEAK: no uppercase letter, common word or too simple
G7#kq!2Lm -> STRONG

cards.en:
Analogy: a strong lock is useless if you use one key for your home, car and office, or tape the key to the door.

Book's habits:

  • change passwords regularly, at least once every three months
  • do not reuse the last 3 passwords
  • do not use the same password on different systems
  • do not record passwords on paper or electronic devices
  • do not send others your passwords; do not share passwords with others

Why no reuse across sites: if one website leaks, attackers try the same email + password on other sites. This is called credential stuffing.

Extra protection: a password manager (one strong master password protects the rest) and 2FA (two-factor authentication: password + a code from your phone).

Exam wording: Change passwords regularly (at least once every three months); do not use the same password on different systems; do not record, send or share passwords.

System-side measures (DSE 2019 1B Q2a): force users to change the password after the first login (avoids leaks of the default password; the password becomes personal). Show the last login date/time and status after login (the user can check whether someone else logged in or tried to).
cards.zh:
比喻：家、车、办公室共用一条锁匙，或把锁匙贴在门上，锁再好也没用。

书中习惯：定期更改，至少每三个月一次；不重用最近 3 个密码；不同系统不用同一密码；不把密码写在纸上或电子设备；不发送、不分享密码。

为何不同网站不用同一密码：一个网站外泄，黑客会拿同一组电邮＋密码去试其他网站，称为 credential stuffing。

额外保护：密码管理器；2FA 双重认证（密码＋手机验证码）。

考试写法：Change passwords regularly (at least once every three months); do not use the same password on different systems; do not record, send or share passwords.

系统方面的措施：首次登入后强制更改密码（避免预设密码外泄，密码个人化）。登入后显示上次登入日期时间及成功／失败（用户可知有没有别人登入或尝试登入）。

ex.q: Why is using one password for email, games and banking dangerous?
ex.a:
1. A small game site is hacked and its passwords leak.
  2. Attackers try the same email + password on email and bank sites (credential stuffing).
  3. All three accounts are lost at once.
  4. Use a different password per system.
ex.az:
1. 小型游戏网站被入侵，密码外泄。
  2. 黑客用同一组资料试电邮和银行（credential stuffing）。
  3. 三个帐户一次失守。
  4. 每个系统用不同密码。

ex.q: Rachel's last passwords were A1, B2, C3 (oldest→newest). The system says 'do not reuse the last 3'. Can she change to B2? To A1?
ex.a:
1. The last 3 are A1, B2, C3.
  2. B2 is in the list → not allowed.
  3. A1 is also in the list → not allowed.
  4. She must choose a new password.
ex.az:
1. 最近 3 个是 A1、B2、C3。
  2. B2 在内 → 不可。
  3. A1 也在内 → 不可。
  4. 须用新密码。

ex.q: A student keeps all passwords in a phone note called 'Passwords' so he won't forget. Good habit?
ex.a:
1. Mistake: the book says do not record passwords on paper or electronic devices.
  2. Anyone who gets the phone (or malware on it) gets every password.
  3. Better: memorable passphrases, or a proper encrypted password manager with 2FA.
ex.az:
1. 错误：书中指不要把密码记在纸上或电子设备。
  2. 别人拿到手机（或手机中毒）就拿到全部密码。
  3. 较好：易记的密码短语，或有加密及 2FA 的密码管理器。

ex.q: Why does a school reading platform show 'Last login: 3 Nov 02:14, failed'?
ex.a: So the user can see whether someone else has tried to log in to the account and react (change password).
ex.az: 让用户知道有没有人试图登入他的帐户。

cards.en:
Analogy: a parcel from an unknown sender that ticks. You don't open it on the kitchen table; you get it checked first.

Why: email is a main channel for malware and phishing.

Rules:

  • Do not open attachments or hyperlinks in suspicious emails.
  • Scan attachments with antivirus before opening, especially .exe, .vbs and .bat files. These are executable/script files: opening them runs a program.
  • Turn on spam filtering.
  • Don't reply to spam (it confirms your address is active).
  • Check the sender's real address, not just the display name.
ExtensionTypeRisk
.exeprogramhigh
.bat / .vbsscripthigh
.jpg / .pdfdocument/imagelower (still scan)

Book example: Ann gets an anonymous email with you.exe "containing her photos". She runs it and nothing appears, because it is a program (likely malware), not a photo.

Exam wording: Do not open attachments or hyperlinks in suspicious emails. Scan attachments, especially those with extensions such as .exe, .vbs and .bat, with antivirus software before opening.

Also: under the Unsolicited Electronic Messages Ordinance, register your number on the Do-not-call Registers to refuse commercial SMS. Most organisations never ask for login details by email or phone: contact the organisation through official channels to verify.
cards.zh:
比喻：陌生人寄来一个会“滴答”响的包裹，不会在厨房直接拆，先拿去检查。

为什么：电邮是恶意软件和钓鱼的主要途径。

规则：不要打开可疑电邮的附件或连结；附件先用防毒软件扫描，特别是 .exe、.vbs、.bat——这些是可执行/脚本文件，打开即执行程式；启用垃圾邮件过滤；不回复 spam；检查真实寄件地址而不只看显示名称。

书例：Ann 收到匿名电邮附 you.exe 说有她的相片，执行后没有相片——因为它是程式（可能是恶意软件）而非图片。

考试写法：Do not open attachments or hyperlinks in suspicious emails. Scan attachments, especially those with extensions such as .exe, .vbs and .bat, with antivirus software before opening.

另外：根据《非应邀电子讯息条例》，可把号码登记在拒收讯息登记册，拒收商业短讯。大部分机构不会用电邮或电话索取登入资料，应经官方渠道向机构核实。

ex.q: Which attachments should be scanned first: report.pdf, run.bat, photo.jpg, setup.exe?
ex.a:
1. run.bat is a script file → runs commands.
  2. setup.exe is an executable program.
  3. Scan these two first (all attachments from unknown senders should still be scanned).
ex.az:
1. run.bat 是脚本，会执行指令。
  2. setup.exe 是可执行程式。
  3. 先扫描这两个（不明来源附件全部都应扫描）。

ex.q: Explain why nothing appeared when Ann opened 'you.exe' from an anonymous email.
ex.a:
1. .exe means it is an executable program, not an image.
  2. Opening it ran the program silently in the background.
  3. It is likely malware (e.g. a trojan) now installed on her PC.
  4. She should disconnect and run a full antivirus scan.
ex.az:
1. .exe 是可执行程式，不是图片。
  2. 打开后程式在背景静静执行。
  3. 很可能是已安装的恶意软件（如木马）。
  4. 应断网并全面扫毒。

ex.q: Ben gets 'invoice.pdf.exe' from a client name he knows and opens it because 'it's a PDF from a known person'. What went wrong?
ex.a:
1. Mistake: the last extension decides the type: '.exe' → it's a program disguised as a PDF.
  2. The display name can be faked; he didn't check the real sender address.
  3. Correct: check the real extension and sender, scan before opening, confirm with the client by phone.
ex.az:
1. 错误：由最后的扩展名决定类型：.exe → 伪装成 PDF 的程式。
  2. 显示名称可伪造，他没检查真实寄件地址。
  3. 正确：看真实扩展名和寄件人，先扫描，致电客户确认。

cards.en:
Analogy: handing out photocopies of your ID card. Once copies are out, you can't collect them back.

Before giving personal information online, ask 4 questions:

  1. Is the purpose of collection stated?
  2. Is each item necessary?
  3. Will the data be transferred to third parties?
  4. How can I access or correct it?

The answers should be in the privacy policy / Personal Information Collection Statement (PICS). Read it.

Good practice:

  • give only the minimum needed; skip optional fields
  • be careful with online forms, lucky draws and quizzes
  • set social media accounts to private
  • never post ID numbers, addresses or travel plans publicly

Exam wording: Read the privacy policy to check the purpose of collection, whether the data is necessary and whether it will be transferred to third parties; provide only the minimum personal information needed.
cards.zh:
比喻：派发身份证副本，派出去就收不回。

提供个人资料前问 4 个问题：①有否说明收集目的？②每项是否必需？③会否转交第三方？④如何查阅或改正？

答案应在私隐政策/收集个人资料声明 (PICS)，要细阅。

好做法：只给最少必要资料，跳过选填；小心网上表格、抽奖、测验；社交帐户设私人；不公开身份证号码、地址、行程。

考试写法：Read the privacy policy to check the purpose of collection, whether the data is necessary and whether it will be transferred to third parties; provide only the minimum personal information needed.

ex.q: A lucky-draw form asks name, phone, HKID number and income. What should you do?
ex.a:
1. Purpose: contacting the winner needs only name + phone.
  2. HKID and income are unnecessary.
  3. Read the PICS: will data be sold to third parties for marketing?
  4. If HKID/income are compulsory, don't join.
ex.az:
1. 联络得奖者只需姓名＋电话。
  2. 身份证和收入不必要。
  3. 读 PICS：会否卖给第三方作推广？
  4. 若必填身份证/收入，不参加。

ex.q: Before her holiday, Joyce wants to post 'Whole family in Japan 1–10 Aug!' publicly with her building's name visible in an old photo. Advise her.
ex.a:
1. Travel plans + address tell burglars the home is empty.
  2. Post after returning, or share only with close friends.
  3. Remove photos that show the building name.
ex.az:
1. 行程＋住址等于告诉小偷家中无人。
  2. 回来后才贴，或只给好友看。
  3. 删除露出大厦名称的相片。

ex.q: A student says: 'The website is famous, so I don't need to read its privacy policy.' Comment.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: big companies also share data with third parties or use it for marketing, and can be hacked.
  2. The policy tells you purpose, transfers and how to access/correct data.
  3. Always check it and give minimum data.
ex.az:
1. 错误：大公司也会把资料给第三方或作推广，也会被入侵。
  2. 政策说明目的、转交对象、查阅改正方法。
  3. 应查看并只给最少资料。

cards.t: HK laws: Telecommunications Ordinance & Crimes Ordinance
cards.tz: 香港法例：电讯条例与刑事罪行条例
cards.en:
Analogy: entering someone's house without permission is trespass; breaking things inside is damage; entering to steal is burglary. The computer laws follow the same idea.

LawWhat it coversKey words
Cap. 106 Telecommunications Ordinance s.27AUnauthorised access to computer by telecommunications: knowingly causing a computer to perform any function to get unauthorised access to a program or data, via telecommunications (e.g. Internet)access without permission; fine
Cap. 200 Crimes Ordinance s.60Destroying or damaging property: "property" includes programs and data in a computer or storage medium; misusing a computer or altering, adding or erasing programs/data counts as damagechange/delete data = damage
Cap. 200 Crimes Ordinance s.161Access to computers with criminal or dishonest intent: intent to deceive, to gain for oneself or another, or to cause loss to anothermax 5 years' imprisonment

How to choose: just got in without permission over a network → s.27A. Changed/deleted data → s.60. Got in to cheat, gain or cause loss → s.161.

Exam wording: Telecommunications Ordinance Section 27A: unauthorised access to computer by telecommunications. Crimes Ordinance Section 60: destroying or damaging property (including data). Section 161: access to computers with criminal or dishonest intent, maximum imprisonment 5 years.

Penalties in the book: s.27A: fine of HK$25,000. s.161: up to 5 years' imprisonment. Book Activity 5.11 answers: installing spyware on public computers → s.60 + s.161; cracking a shareware trial so it never expires → s.60 + s.161 + s.27A; hacking a web server and changing content → s.60 + s.161; QR code leading to malicious sites → s.161 (plus s.60 and s.27A if malware is installed).
cards.zh:
比喻：未经许可入屋是擅闯；在屋内破坏是损坏；入屋偷东西是爆窃。电脑法例同一道理。

法例内容关键
Cap. 106《电讯条例》第 27A 条藉电讯而未获授权取用电脑：明知而经电讯（如互联网）令电脑执行功能以未授权存取程式或数据未经许可进入；罚款
Cap. 200《刑事罪行条例》第 60 条摧毁或损坏财产：财产包括电脑及储存媒体内的程式与数据；误用电脑、更改/加入/删除程式数据均属损坏改/删数据＝损坏
Cap. 200 第 161 条有犯罪或不诚实意图而取用电脑：意图欺骗、为自己或他人获利、令他人损失最高监禁 5 年

判断：只是经网络未经许可进入 → 27A；改/删数据 → 60；为欺骗、获利、令人损失而进入 → 161。

考试写法：Telecommunications Ordinance Section 27A: unauthorised access to computer by telecommunications. Crimes Ordinance Section 60: destroying or damaging property (including data). Section 161: access to computers with criminal or dishonest intent, maximum imprisonment 5 years.

课本罚则：第 27A 条：罚款 HK$25,000；第 161 条：最高监禁 5 年。活动 5.11 答案：在公用电脑装间谍软件 → 第 60 + 161 条；破解共享软件试用期 → 第 60 + 161 + 27A 条；入侵伺服器改网页 → 第 60 + 161 条；QR code 导去恶意网站 → 第 161 条（若装了恶意软件再加 60 及 27A）。

ex.q: A student guesses a teacher's password over the Internet and changes his own marks. Which provisions apply?
ex.a:
1. Logged in without permission via the Internet → Telecommunications Ordinance s.27A.
  2. Altered data (marks) → Crimes Ordinance s.60 (damaging property).
  3. Did it to gain for himself / deceive → Crimes Ordinance s.161 (dishonest intent, up to 5 years).
ex.az:
1. 经互联网未经许可登入 → 27A。
  2. 更改分数数据 → 第 60 条。
  3. 为自己得益/欺骗 → 第 161 条（最高 5 年）。

ex.q: An ex-employee logs in remotely with an old account and deletes the company's customer files out of anger. Which laws?
ex.a:
1. Remote login without authorisation → s.27A.
  2. Deleting data = damaging property → s.60.
  3. Intent to cause loss to another → s.161.
ex.az:
1. 远程未授权登入 → 27A。
  2. 删除数据＝损坏财产 → 60。
  3. 意图令他人损失 → 161。

ex.q: A student writes: 'Deleting someone's files isn't a crime because files aren't physical property.' Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: under Crimes Ordinance s.60, 'property' includes programs and data in a computer or storage medium.
  2. Altering, adding or erasing data counts as damage.
  3. So it can be a criminal offence.
ex.az:
1. 错误：第 60 条中“财产”包括电脑内的程式和数据。
  2. 更改、加入、删除数据都属损坏。
  3. 所以可属刑事罪行。

ex.q: John uses Josh's password from a sticky note to log in and change his profile icon as a prank. Which crime?
ex.a: Access to computers with criminal or dishonest intent (s.161) / unauthorised access by telecommunications (s.27A); changing data may also count as damaging property (s.60).
ex.az: 未经授权存取（27A）／不诚实意图存取（161）；改资料亦可能属损坏财产（60）。

cards.tz: 香港法例：私隐条例与非应邀电子讯息条例
cards.en:
Analogy: PDPO is the rulebook for anyone who keeps a "file" on you. UEMO is the "No junk mail" sign on your mailbox that senders must respect.

Cap. 486 Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance (PDPO): six data protection principles control how data users (organisations holding data) collect, process and use personal data:

  1. Collection: lawful and fair means; collect only what is necessary. Before collecting, tell the data subject (the person) whether it is compulsory, the purpose, who it may go to, and the right to access/correct.
  2. Accuracy and retention: keep it accurate; keep no longer than necessary.
  3. Use: do not use for purposes other than the original purpose without consent.
  4. Security: protect against unauthorised access, loss or leaks.
  5. Openness: make policies available.
  6. Access and correction: data subjects can access and correct their data.

Direct marketing / giving data to a third party needs prior notice and consent: up to HK$500,000 and 3 years (HK$1,000,000 and 5 years if provided for gain). Disclosing personal data without consent to gain or cause harm (doxing) is also an offence.

Cap. 593 Unsolicited Electronic Messages Ordinance (UEMO) (effective 22 Dec 2007): people may refuse commercial electronic messages (fax, email, SMS, pre-recorded calls). It does not cover person-to-person real-time calls. Offenders may be fined or jailed; victims may claim compensation.

Exam wording: The PDPO lists six data protection principles; personal data must not be used for purposes other than the original purpose without consent. The UEMO allows recipients to refuse commercial electronic messages.

Penalties in the book: breaking the direct-marketing rules: up to HK$500,000 fine and 3 years' prison; giving data to a third party for gain: up to HK$1 million and 5 years. Disclosing personal data obtained without consent to gain, cause loss or psychological harm (doxing): up to HK$1 million and 5 years. UEMO (Cap. 593) took effect on 22 December 2007; covers faxes, emails, SMS, pre-recorded phone messages, but not person-to-person real-time calls; victims can seek compensation.
cards.zh:
比喻：私隐条例是所有持有你“档案”的机构要守的规则；非应邀讯息条例像信箱上“请勿投寄广告”的告示，发送者必须遵守。

Cap. 486《个人资料（私隐）条例》：六项保障资料原则规管资料使用者如何收集、处理、使用个人资料：

  1. 收集：合法公平、只收必需；收集前告知资料当事人是否必须提供、目的、可能转交对象、查阅及改正权。
  2. 准确及保留：保持准确，保留不超过所需。
  3. 使用：未经同意不得用于原本目的以外。
  4. 保安：防止未授权存取、遗失、外泄。
  5. 透明：公开政策。
  6. 查阅及改正：当事人可查阅和改正。

直接促销/提供给第三方须事先通知并取得同意：最高罚 50 万及监禁 3 年（为得益提供：100 万及 5 年）。未经同意披露资料以图利或造成伤害（起底）亦属违法。

Cap. 593《非应邀电子讯息条例》（2007 年 12 月 22 日生效）：可拒收商业电子讯息（传真、电邮、短讯、预录电话），不涵盖人对人实时通话；违者可被罚款或监禁，受害人可索偿。

考试写法：The PDPO lists six data protection principles; personal data must not be used for purposes other than the original purpose without consent. The UEMO allows recipients to refuse commercial electronic messages.

课本罚则：违反直接促销规定：最高罚款 50 万元及监禁 3 年；为得益把资料提供给第三者：最高 100 万元及 5 年。未经同意披露个人资料以图利、造成损失或心理伤害（起底）：最高 100 万元及 5 年。《非应邀电子讯息条例》（第 593 章）于 2007 年 12 月 22 日生效，涵盖传真、电邮、短讯、预录电话讯息，但不包括真人实时通话；受害人可索偿。

ex.q: Classify: (1) selling customer data to other companies secretly (2) sending ad emails after the recipient refused.
ex.a:
1. (1) Providing personal data to third parties without notice/consent, for gain → PDPO (Cap. 486); up to HK$1,000,000 and 5 years.
  2. (2) Commercial electronic messages after refusal → UEMO (Cap. 593).
ex.az:
1. (1) 未经通知同意把资料提供给第三方图利 → 私隐条例；最高 100 万及 5 年。
  2. (2) 拒收后仍发商业电邮 → Cap. 593。

ex.q: A gym collected members' phone numbers for class reminders, then used them to send insurance offers from a partner. Which principle is broken?
ex.a:
1. Original purpose: class reminders.
  2. New use: direct marketing for another company.
  3. Breaks the use principle (no use beyond the original purpose without consent) and the direct-marketing consent rule.
ex.az:
1. 原本目的：上课提示。
  2. 新用途：为另一公司直接促销。
  3. 违反使用原则（未经同意不得用于原本目的以外）及直接促销同意规定。

ex.q: A student says: 'A salesperson phoned me live after I said no, so it breaks the UEMO.' Is this right?
ex.a:
1. Mistake: the UEMO covers fax, email, SMS and pre-recorded calls.
  2. It does not cover person-to-person real-time calls.
  3. So a live salesperson call is not covered by the UEMO (it would be if it were a recorded message).
ex.az:
1. 错误：UEMO 涵盖传真、电邮、短讯及预录电话。
  2. 不涵盖人对人实时通话。
  3. 所以真人推销电话不受 UEMO 规管（预录讯息才受）。

mc.q: Which malware attaches itself to executable files and activates when the file is run?
mc.e: A virus needs a host file and is activated when the host is executed.
mc.ez: Virus 依附宿主文件，执行时启动。

mc.e: Worms self-replicate and spread over networks automatically.

mc.q: Which statement about Trojan programs is correct?
mc.e: Trojans lure users by looking useful; they do not self-replicate.

mc.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a Trojan program?
o: It can self-replicate to all contacts
mc.e: Self-replication to contacts describes a worm.
mc.ez: 自我复制是 worm 特征。

mc.q: The main purpose of spyware is to
mc.e: Spyware collects data such as keystrokes and passwords while hiding.

mc.q: A keylogger that records every keystroke is a type of
mc.e: Recording keyboard input to steal data is spyware.

Files on a PC are encrypted and a message demands Bitcoin for the key. This is

o: Disconnect from the network, report to police and restore from backup
Copy the encrypted files to another PC and open them

mc.e: DoS exhausts resources so users cannot get service.

Why is a DDoS attack harder to block than a DoS attack from one computer?
o: Traffic comes from many different IP addresses
mc.e: Blocking one IP is not enough.

mc.q: How does antivirus software identify known malware?
o: By comparing files with virus signatures

mc.q: Why should antivirus automatic update be enabled?
o: To recognise the latest malware signatures

mc.q: Which information does a firewall check in data packets?
mc.e: Rules are based on IP, port, type etc.

mc.q: Which is an advantage of a software firewall over a hardware firewall?
o: Lower cost and easier to install
mc.e: Software firewalls are cheap and easy, but protect one device.

mc.q: Which is TRUE about a hardware firewall?
o: It costs less than software firewalls
It is a program installed on each PC
It writes a firewall program into a chip and is more efficient
It can only protect one device

o: Legally attacks systems to find security bugs

mc.e: Dynamic pages contain client-side scripts run by the browser.

sq.q: Malware types.

parts.q: Distinguish a virus and a worm in terms of how they spread.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Virus attaches to executable files/documents and spreads when the infected host is executed/copied [1]
Worm needs no host file and spreads through the network by itself (e.g. emails itself to contacts) [1]

parts.q: State ONE difference between a Trojan program and a virus.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Trojan disguises as useful software and does not self-replicate, while a virus self-replicates [1]

parts.q: Describe how ransomware affects a victim and give TWO preventive measures.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Encrypts the victim's files and demands ransom for decryption [1]
Regular (offline) backup [1]
Update OS / antivirus / firewall / avoid suspicious attachments [1]

sq.q: Jenny's computer becomes slow, shows many pop-up ads and her home page has changed.

parts.q: Name the most likely type of malware.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Adware (may also be spyware) [1]

parts.q: Suggest TWO ways she can remove it and prevent recurrence.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Run an updated antivirus/anti-spyware scan and remove it [1]
Remove suspicious browser plug-ins / disable pop-ups / download only from official sources [1]

parts.q: Explain why spyware is often unnoticed.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
It does not damage the system and hides itself to avoid detection while collecting data [1]

sq.q: An online shop's website becomes unavailable during a sale. Thousands of computers around the world sent requests at the same time.

parts.q: Name the attack.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
DDoS (Distributed Denial-of-Service) attack [1]

parts.q: Explain the role of zombie computers.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Hacked computers remotely controlled by the hacker [1]
Send large numbers of requests to the server simultaneously without owners' knowledge, exhausting its resources [1]

parts.q: Suggest ONE way home users can avoid their PCs becoming zombies.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Install/update antivirus and firewall; patch OS [1]

sq.q: Tom uses free Wi-Fi in a café to log in to his bank account.

parts.q: Describe how a man-in-the-middle attack could happen here.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Hacker sets up a fake hotspot / sits between Tom and the bank [1]
Intercepts or tampers with data, e.g. captures login details or redirects to a fake site [1]

parts.q: Suggest TWO measures Tom should take.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Use a VPN [1]
Use mobile data / only HTTPS and check certificate / avoid banking on public Wi-Fi [1]

sq.q: A school wants to improve the security of its network.

parts.q: Compare a hardware firewall and a software firewall and recommend one for the school.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Hardware: chip-based device, protects whole network, more efficient/stable but costly [1]
Software: installed on each device, cheaper/easier but protects only that device [1]
Recommend hardware firewall at gateway (plus software on PCs) [1]

parts.q: Explain how antivirus software detects malware and why automatic update is needed.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Compares files with virus signatures in database [1]
Update to recognise newly discovered malware [1]

parts.q: Explain authentication, authorisation and accounting using the school's e-class system.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Authentication: verify identity via login ID/password [1]
Authorisation: students view, teachers edit [1]
Accounting: logs of who accessed/changed data [1]

sq.q: Mr Chan sets up Wi-Fi for his family.

parts.q: Which encryption protocol should he choose among WEP, WPA and WPA2? Explain.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
WPA2 [1]; most secure, higher security standard than WPA (TKIP changing key) and WEP (easily cracked) [1]

parts.q: Describe TWO additional settings to prevent unauthorised devices from connecting.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Turn off SSID broadcast so the name is hidden [1]
MAC address filtering whitelist [1]

parts.q: Give ONE limitation of MAC address filtering.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
MAC addresses can be spoofed / inconvenient to add new devices [1]

sq.q: A company lets staff work from home.

parts.q: Explain how a VPN protects data sent between home and the office.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Creates a tunnel between the device and the VPN server [1]
Packets are encrypted so intercepted data cannot be read [1]

parts.q: Name the type of VPN used and ONE other application of VPN.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Remote access VPN [1]
Intranet VPN linking branch LANs / accessing WAN securely [1]

sq.q: Social engineering.

parts.q: Define social engineering.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Manipulating trust or greed to trick victims into disclosing confidential information [1]

parts.q: For each scenario name the attack: (i) a USB labelled 'Salary 2026' left in the office; (ii) a fake online lover asking for money; (iii) a caller claiming to be your friend asking for a verification code.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
(i) Baiting [1]
(ii) Catfishing [1]
(iii) Pretexting [1]

parts.q: Suggest TWO ways to identify a phishing email.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Sender domain/URL not official or misspelt [1]
Urgent request for passwords/payment via link [1]

sq.q: Online privacy on a public computer.

parts.q: Describe how cookies may threaten privacy.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Websites store records of user operations/login on the device [1]
Third-party cookies track activity across sites; next user may access logged-in session [1]

parts.q: Suggest THREE measures to keep anonymous when using a library computer.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Use private browsing [1]
Turn off autofill / don't save passwords [1]
Clear history and cookies; log out [1]

parts.q: Explain why private browsing does not make Tom anonymous to his ISP, and suggest a solution.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Packets still contain his IP address, so the ISP can record activity [1]
Use a proxy server or VPN [1]

sq.q: Passwords and laws.

parts.q: State FOUR rules for creating a strong password.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
At least 8 characters; mix of number, upper, lower, special character; no personal information; no simple/common words (any four, 0.5 each)

parts.q: Explain why the same password should not be used on different systems.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
If one system leaks, attackers can access the others [1]

parts.q: Name the Hong Kong ordinance violated: (i) selling customer data without consent; (ii) sending ads after refusal; (iii) hacking a computer with intent to cheat.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
(i) Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance [1]
(ii) Unsolicited Electronic Messages Ordinance [1]
(iii) Crimes Ordinance s.161 [1]

pr.task: Write is_strong(pw, personal) that returns True only if the password follows the textbook rules: at least 8 characters; contains at least 1 digit, 1 uppercase letter, 1 lowercase letter and 1 special character (any character that is not a letter or digit); does not contain any string in the list personal (case-insensitive); and does not contain the common word 'password' or '123456' (case-insensitive).
